title: GitHub Ultimate — project direction and first milestone
description: Self-contained project intake. The three decision sections contain the research findings and tradeoffs; no repository browsing or separate report is needed. All choices are checkboxes. Select the options you want; where labels identify alternatives in one group, pick one preferred direction or explain your combination in the section notes. Leave uncertain groups unanswered and say what needs discussion.

allowCodeFileChanges.allowLabel: Submit and allow implementation of the agreed first slice
allowCodeFileChanges.avoidLabel: Submit for discussion only — avoid code/file changes
allowCodeFileChanges.description: This controls what the next agent may do after processing your response. Discussion-only means no code/file edits. Allowing implementation is not authorization to publish an extension, dispatch a paid agent job, change repository settings, or push commits. Those live operations must follow the execution policy you choose below.

questions.title: 1. Who is this for, and what must the first milestone demonstrate?
questions.description:
The project vision is a TypeScript browser extension that enhances GitHub itself: PRs/issues are human-agent workspaces; the homepage monitors workflows; Notifications becomes an attention inbox; GitHub Actions runs agents; Markdown plus YAML carries forms. GitHub stores the canonical records, so there is no dedicated application backend and no paid Copilot dependency. The existing github-ultimate repository currently has only a README and an MIT license.

The proposed first working loop is: a form in a PR comment → extension renders it → human fills it → extension populates GitHub's native comment editor → human clicks Comment → a trusted default-branch Actions workflow runs one approved coding agent → a structured result comment links the task and workflow. Every answer starts a new agent execution. Select an Audience option, a First milestone option, and a Platform option; optional scope additions can also be selected. Personal-account support does not automatically mean this is only for your own use.

choices.label: Audience: myself and a small personal-account beta
choices.description: Start with unpacked Chrome installation, one sandbox repository and documented setup. Keep public store distribution and broader onboarding as later milestones.
choices.is_recommended_reason: Matches the concept-stage intake and keeps the first workflow demonstrable without a release program.

choices.label: Audience: other users from the first release
choices.description: Include reproducible onboarding, GitHub App ownership/installation instructions, extension packaging, privacy documentation and distribution expectations in the first release. Specify Chrome Web Store/TestFlight/App Store expectations in notes.

choices.label: First milestone: complete PR form → agent → structured result loop
choices.description: Prioritize a versioned form, native comment submission, trusted Actions executor and correlated response. A second form from the agent and a human answer should prove the human-in-the-loop design. Add OAuth, dashboard and editing afterward.
choices.is_recommended_reason: Proves the project's differentiator before investing in account-wide dashboards or editor polish.

choices.label: First milestone: desktop Monaco editing first
choices.description: Prioritize a newly implemented Monaco bridge for Markdown comments/descriptions, preserving native submit, quote reply, attachments, drafts and keyboard behavior. The agent loop follows. The old Monaco discovery only wraps issue_body and gollum-editor-body despite broader README claims, so modern GitHub coverage must be rebuilt and tested.

choices.label: First milestone: workflow dashboard and GitHub App auth first
choices.description: Prioritize connection and running/queued/completed/failed runs on github.com. Actions runs are repository-scoped, so begin with explicitly selected repositories, bounded concurrency and rate-aware visible-page refresh. The form/agent loop follows; a dashboard cannot cheaply assume an account-wide runs endpoint.

choices.label: Platform: Chrome first, with an early Safari forms/auth spike
choices.description: Use Chrome MV3 for the first acceptance demo, share browser-independent logic, and probe Safari iOS device authorization, suspension and mobile forms early. Full iOS app packaging follows the desktop loop. On iPhone prefer native editing initially; desktop Monaco assets are large and mobile keyboard/layout behavior is unverified.
choices.is_recommended_reason: Surfaces the core cross-platform constraints without making Xcode/device packaging block the first end-to-end result.

choices.label: Platform: Chrome and a real iPhone are both first-milestone gates
choices.description: Include Safari Web Extension conversion, an iOS host app, signing/Xcode or TestFlight setup, real-device navigation/forms/auth tests and mobile-safe UI before declaring the first milestone complete. Specify available Mac/iPhone/signing access in notes.

choices.label: Optional scope: also recreate Commit Lens commit-list enhancements
choices.description: Commit Lens adds changed-file counts, additions/deletions, signature/merge indicators, compact rows and per-day counts. The intake primarily references it for auth rather than requiring these features. Selecting this explicitly adds a separate feature track; its implementation cannot currently be copied without permission.

choices.label: Optional scope: slash commands in the first user-facing release
choices.description: The vision mentions slash commands but gives no grammar or interaction design. Commands should select the same repository-approved actions and produce the same task records as forms, without arbitrary workflow/endpoint execution. Give two or three desired commands in notes.

choices.label: Later roadmap: homepage command center and Notifications work inbox
choices.description: Retain running/failed/attention widgets and Needs input / Running / Ready for review / Failed / Done states after the first loop. Canonical state must live in GitHub records, not notification read/unread status. Refresh on open/visible views first; iOS and suspended MV3 workers cannot promise continuous monitoring.

questions.title: 2. What should we reuse, and how compatible should GitHub forms be with BeadsForm?
questions.description:
Static source review on 2026-11-05: Commit Lens at 69fd101 has no license file or package license; GitHub reports no detected license. The archived Monaco extension at cb32dd4 explicitly declares UNLICENSED and has no license file. Public source/forking is not a redistribution grant. A fresh TypeScript extension is therefore the proposed foundation; adopting the separately licensed Monaco Editor dependency is a different decision from copying the extension.

The checked-out vibe-dashboard has an Apache-2.0 root license and a small portable package, packages/beads-form/src/index.ts, separated from Springboard server routes and Node bead storage. Its package is private, version 0.0.0. Standard BeadsForm questions are choices (always MULTI-SELECT checkboxes), text and textarea, with descriptions, recommendations and automatically generated notes. Answers to choices normalize to option-ID booleans. It does not currently provide the intake's select/radio/default-value fields, YAML fields syntax or strict untrusted-schema validation. A controls metadata type naming radio/select is not public authoring support. The compiler escapes content but is not by itself a complete malicious-input validator.

The intake instead proposes a fenced github-task block containing YAML frontmatter: version, title, fields (text/textarea/select/checkbox/radio, required/default/options), followed by Markdown task instructions. Regardless of syntax, forms cannot specify arbitrary JavaScript, API endpoints, workflow names or privileged execution operations. Presentation and execution authorization stay separate. The product can keep all persistent state in GitHub comments without requiring beads or the dashboard at runtime. Select a Reuse policy, a Schema direction, and a Runtime relationship; add continuity policy if acceptable.

choices.label: Reuse policy: fresh implementation; references supply lessons
choices.description: Independently implement navigation, auth and editor integration. Do not copy the two unlicensed extensions. Reuse the Apache form package only if the schema choice calls for it, retaining applicable notices and recording provenance. No need to delay the first milestone while awaiting upstream replies.
choices.is_recommended_reason: Both extension reuse permissions are absent today; a new architecture also avoids their legacy integration problems.

choices.label: Reuse policy: seek explicit upstream permission before a port
choices.description: Track permission/license clarification for Commit Lens and/or the Monaco extension and identify exactly which components would be reused. Keep copying/redistributing those components gated on a grant. State whether waiting should block the milestone; requesting permission externally is separate from this planning response.

choices.label: Schema: BeadsForm-compatible question/answer subset inside GitHub YAML
choices.description: Use a versioned github-task envelope whose presentation uses BeadsForm's choices/text/textarea IDs, descriptions, recommendation reasons and option-boolean answers. YAML serializes these objects; GitHub-specific task/action references live outside presentation. Adapt or vendor the portable Apache package with strict validation. Selects, radios and defaults become explicit later protocol work.
choices.is_recommended_reason: Provides a concrete reuse boundary and familiar agent-generated decision forms while keeping the first schema small.

choices.label: Schema: implement the intake's full fields syntax immediately
choices.description: Ship text, textarea, select, checkbox, radio groups, required validation and defaults in schema v1 as described in the issue. Build an independent renderer or an explicit adapter; document which forms cannot round-trip into today's BeadsForm DSL rather than claiming exact compatibility. More controls and default/answer semantics need fixtures up front.

choices.label: Schema: evolve a shared BeadsForm package for both projects first
choices.description: Coordinate additions for single-select/defaults and strict schema validation upstream, define versioning/publication, and consume a pinned package in the extension and dashboard. This gives deeper compatibility but introduces cross-repository changes and release coordination. Specify whether you want those dashboard source edits authorized in the notes.

choices.label: Runtime: GitHub-only records; beads/dashboard remain authoring tools
choices.description: Forms, answers and task status are stored in PR/issue comments so another browser can reconstruct them. Reuse UI/protocol concepts without depending on dashboard RPC, local filesystem paths or a running beads service. Keep credentials in the privileged extension context and drafts/preferences in local storage.
choices.is_recommended_reason: Preserves the intake's no-dedicated-backend requirement and makes the workspace usable across devices.

choices.label: Runtime: also design a beads/dashboard interoperability bridge
choices.description: Keep GitHub as canonical task state but add explicit import/export or bead-ID mapping for dashboard workflows. Define direction/conflict rules and whether this is file-based tooling or an online bridge. An always-running dashboard bridge changes deployment assumptions and should be specified before implementation.

choices.label: Continuity: stable IDs, revision-bound answers and linked follow-up tasks
choices.description: Record schema/task/form/response IDs, source comment and revision/hash, repository, issue-or-PR number, requester, applicable PR head SHA, parent task and execution attempt. Workflows post task ID plus run URL instead of guessing a matching run by branch/time. Reject edited/deleted/stale source forms; an answer to a follow-up creates a new linked execution. Define changed-PR-head behavior before execution, and keep raw Markdown readable without the extension.
choices.is_recommended_reason: Supports cross-device reconstruction, duplicate handling and asynchronous agent questions with auditable provenance.

questions.title: 3. Which agent, authorization policy and backend-free auth path should we prove?
questions.description:
For the first loop, the extension can populate the existing comment editor and let you click GitHub's Comment button; no extension API token is needed. A repository-installed issue_comment workflow runs from trusted default-branch configuration and must independently verify requester permissions, original form/revision and allowed action. Untrusted comment fields must never become shell code, arbitrary workflow names or secret-bearing privileged PR execution. A valid-looking result comment is not proof it came from the trusted workflow.

Commit Lens's auth lessons need correction: it reads tokens in its content script and renders a token input in page DOM; sign-out leaves refresh credentials/alarms; its cache retains failed requests; staggered batches are not a true concurrency cap. Our implementation should keep authenticated API requests/tokens in a privileged background context, expose only typed allowlisted operations, serialize refresh, clear all auth state on sign-out and discard late responses from cancelled sessions.

Crucially, current GitHub documentation says client_secret is NOT required to refresh a GitHub App user token generated via device flow. Commit Lens says a proxy is always needed, which is outdated relative to those docs. The proposed spike tests direct device authorization plus secretless refresh in packaged Chrome and Safari; it must verify real behavior, token rotation and suspension instead of assuming success. GitHub App access is the intersection of user permissions and installed repository permissions. Private runs need Actions read; direct dispatch later needs Actions write; PR conversation comments require the applicable Issues/Pull requests permission for the chosen endpoint.

Each agent CLI must be checked for supported noninteractive execution, credentials, licensing and Actions compatibility. Consumer chat subscriptions do not automatically grant model API access. Actions minutes/runner limits differ for public/private repos, and model usage may be billed separately. Select a Dispatch path, one initial Executor (or Mock), an Output mode, an Authorization policy, and an Auth direction. Provide the sandbox owner/repo, agent/model access and timeout/cost limits in Additional notes; never enter secrets.

choices.label: Dispatch: native comment submission before extension OAuth
choices.description: Human previews a structured answer, then submits through GitHub. Trusted issue_comment workflow validates and executes it, posts an acknowledgement with task/run IDs, then a result. Duplicate deliveries and reruns must not create unintended executions; explicit retries get new attempt IDs.
choices.is_recommended_reason: Smallest backend-free vertical slice and the intake's recommended order.

choices.label: Dispatch: authenticated workflow_dispatch in the first milestone
choices.description: Bring GitHub App device auth and Actions write forward, then dispatch only a repository-approved workflow with validated inputs. The workflow still verifies the task and requester; auth is not a replacement for repository policy. Keep a native-comment path if credential-free use remains required.

choices.label: Executor: OpenCode first
choices.description: Implement one pinned noninteractive OpenCode adapter after confirming CLI flags, provider/model credential requirements, output format and license. Keep the runtime allowlisted; do not build adapters for every agent up front. Record model access and an approved repository in notes.

choices.label: Executor: Codex first
choices.description: Implement one pinned noninteractive Codex adapter after checking the actual CLI/auth/runtime contract and available credentials. A paid Copilot subscription is not required. Record the intended model/auth arrangement in notes; do not assume your chat subscription can fund unattended API runs.

choices.label: Executor: Claude Code first
choices.description: Verify current supported unattended invocation, authentication/usage terms and Actions runtime before implementing one adapter. Store credentials in repository Actions secrets, never comments or extension payloads.

choices.label: Executor: deterministic mock first, then choose the real agent
choices.description: Use a fixture executor to prove form parsing, native comment submission, workflow validation, task/run correlation and follow-up rendering without model billing. This is an intermediate infrastructure demo, not completion of the real-agent milestone.

choices.label: Output: analysis-only results and follow-up forms initially
choices.description: Agent may inspect the approved source snapshot and post findings/questions, with a bounded runtime. No direct commits or merges. Separate source inspection from privileged posting and keep model credentials away from untrusted PR scripts. Add write access as a later explicit capability.
choices.is_recommended_reason: Demonstrates structured collaboration while keeping the first workflow's credential and write surface small.

choices.label: Output: propose code on a dedicated branch in the first loop
choices.description: Add scoped Contents write, branch ownership/protection, exact source-SHA checks and attributable commits or a PR. Never write to the default branch or merge automatically. Fork PRs/untrusted code need an isolated read/build path before privileged publishing. Describe the expected change-review flow in notes.

choices.label: Authorization: repository collaborators/maintainers may execute
choices.description: Validate the comment author's current repository permission against a trusted allowlist/minimum role, plus approved form/action IDs. External contributors may see/fill forms but cannot directly trigger credentialed runs. Reject unauthorized/tampered/stale submissions with a clear result, and authenticate agent-result provenance.
choices.is_recommended_reason: A concrete policy that can be independently enforced by the workflow instead of trusting the extension UI or author_association alone.

choices.label: Authorization: allow external requests only after maintainer approval
choices.description: Create a waiting-for-approval state; a current authorized maintainer must approve an exact immutable submission before the privileged workflow runs. Specify who can approve and how changed answers invalidate approval. This adds state/UI/workflow work beyond the collaborator-only prototype.

choices.label: Auth: prove GitHub App device flow and secretless refresh directly
choices.description: Use your own App registration/client ID, test current GitHub documented device-flow refresh without client_secret, token rotation, revocation, denied private repos and packaged-browser suspension. Handle unavailable refresh with explicit reconnect. No client secret belongs in the extension, page DOM, comments or logs; no proxy is assumed.
choices.is_recommended_reason: Current docs support a backend-free refresh path; verify it rather than copying Commit Lens's unnecessary proxy requirement.

choices.label: Auth: defer connection until the comment/agent loop works
choices.description: The first form loop works via native GitHub submission. Schedule the direct auth spike next, before private workflow dashboards/API dispatch; do not promise cross-repository private monitoring in the credential-free prototype. This can be combined with the direct-spike direction to specify ordering.

questions.title: Additional notes — concrete setup, constraints and corrections
questions.description: Master notes for everything not captured above. Suggested template: preferred first milestone and what counts as done; sandbox owner/repo and public/private status; first agent/provider/model and whether appropriate unattended credentials are available (no secret values); approved execution timeout/Actions/model budget; who may trigger runs; changed-PR-head policy; available Mac/iPhone/signing setup; desired Monaco fields or slash commands; repository count and refresh expectations; any priority or architecture corrections. If you selected competing alternatives, state your preferred sequence. Source intake: https://github.com/mickmister/github-ultimate/issues/1. Research snapshot: 2026-11-05. Findings in this form are static source/document review, not claims of a tested live browser or agent deployment.
